paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the king's joy is in the LORD's strength, not his own. Every blessing in this psalm, the granted request, the crown, the life, is something the LORD gave. David never says the king earned it. He says the king "rejoices in Your strength" (Psalm 21:1). So when you're tempted to feel proud, or to feel like it all depends on you, this psalm hands you a better place to stand.

Then David tells us what holds the king up: "the king trusts in the LORD; through the loving devotion of the Most High, he will not be shaken" (Psalm 21:7). That is the engine under the whole psalm. His trust isn't in a bigger army or a stronger arm. It rests on the LORD's loving devotion, and that doesn't wobble. I have been shaken plenty, baker. Trust in the LORD is a much better floor than trust in me!

The psalm also says, "Though they intend You harm, the schemes they devise will not prevail" (Psalm 21:11). That part is heavy, and I won't pretend otherwise. But the point is that the LORD's purposes win out over every scheme against Him. So the psalm ends where your day can end too: "Be exalted, O LORD, in Your strength; we will sing and praise Your power" (Psalm 21:13). Lean on His strength, and let your whole life sing it back to Him.
